Q1.question: Project purpose and why it exists
Q1.value: Canonical source of the Artisyn Implementation Harness — an AI-first engineering lifecycle system (skills, agents, conventions) that runs this platform's own development and is bootstrapped into other projects via docs/Harness/package/. Also ships the ADLC Discovery Tool docs site itself.

Q2.question: Languages, frameworks, runtime, datastore, cloud; propose from config
Q2.value: Node.js >=24, TypeScript, yarn 4 (Berry) workspaces, Nx monorepo; VitePress 1.x/Vite for docs; AWS CDK for infra; AWS Lambda@Edge (Node.js/TS) for auth; AWS CloudFront + S3 as runtime targets. No datastore beyond AWS Secrets Manager for credentials.

Q3.value: Web (apps/docs-web), Auth (apps/lambda-auth), Infrastructure (apps/infra), plus Discuss (client-side giscus comments widget, no infra of its own) documented in HLD/LLD but missing from the CLAUDE.md architecture table
Q3.question: Named containers/layers; drives CONTAINER_LIST and specialist scope

Q4.question: Primary data flow and integrations
Q4.value: Browser → CloudFront (Lambda@Edge auth gate) → S3 (VitePress static build). Discuss container integrates client-side with giscus.app/GitHub Discussions.

Q5.question: Tracker (Jira/Linear/GitHub Issues/none); ticket prefix, tracker URL, optional Confluence/board details
Q5.value: Jira, project key ND, tracker URL https://support.dataart.com (e.g. ND-230). Corrected by developer 2026-09-15 — originally recorded as 'no external tracker' with informal ADLC-NNN references; scrum-master agent deployed and dev/design skills' tracker delegation steps restored accordingly. Confluence URL, transition IDs, labels taxonomy, and team-composition notes not yet provided — left as explicit TODOs in .claude/agents/scrum-master.md pending developer input or MCP lookup once Atlassian credentials are filled in.

Q6.question: Claude Code/Codex CLI/Cursor/Kiro/Windsurf/multiple; select installation paths and exactly one project instruction destination
Q6.value: Claude Code only. Root instruction file: CLAUDE.md (canonical, no AGENTS.md or tool wrapper).

Q7.question: Commit format, branch naming, build/check commands, guarded commands
Q7.value: Commit: `<type>(<scope>): <what changed>` (feat/fix/docs/refactor/test/chore). Branch: `<type>/short-description`. Package manager: yarn only (never npm/npx). Guarded commands (never run directly, present as instructions): `cdk deploy`, `yarn nx run infra:provision`, `git push`, `yarn nx run harness-bootstrap-e2e:agent-e2e`.
Q7.source: CLAUDE.md, docs/Engineering Guide/01 Conventions.md; agent-e2e added as guarded 2026-10-01 (developer request)

Q8.question: Confirmed NFR targets: availability, latency, residency, accessibility, cost, etc.
Q8.value: Already documented: NFR-1..NFR-6 (basic auth on all routes, no hardcoded credentials, region never hardcoded, IaC via CDK, VitePress dead-link build gate, giscus comment-posting permission gating). Constraints: no cost ceiling, small team (~10 internal users), fixed-duration engagement.

Q9.question: Team, pace, risks, other constraints
Q9.value: Small internal team (~10 users), fixed-duration engagement, no defined cost ceiling. No further team/pace detail found in repo evidence.

Q10.question: Enabled Dev/Design/Skill/Architecture lifecycles; default all, Dev required
Q10.value: All four lifecycles enabled: Dev (/dev), Design (/design), Skill (/skill-*), Architecture (/war).

Q10b.question: If Design: Project-scoped (default), Product-context-scoped, or Two-track
Q10b.value: Two-track. Corrected by developer 2026-09-15 — this repo needs both its own Target Architecture (HLD) AND a shared cross-project product-context layer (docs/Harness/, since this repo also bootstraps the harness into other projects), chosen per design session.

Q10c.question: If Product-context or Two-track: shared folder under project:docs/
Q10c.value: Harness (i.e. docs/Harness/ — the existing harness product/handbook documentation, reused as the shared product-context layer)

Q11.question: Azure/AWS/GCP/custom WAF with explicit pillars, or None
Q11.value: AWS Well-Architected Framework, standard pillars (Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability). Matches CLAUDE.md's /war-design description and the all-AWS deployment target.
